# Every Feature in a generated inventory has a passing test, and code coverage and mutants are signals

"Every feature is tested" is checked against a **Feature inventory**: one committed list, generated by `xtask codegen`, of ADR 0037's matrix rows, each area spec's user stories, and every contract the code defines (operations, Error codes, events, settings, CLI commands, exit codes, formats, Plugin kinds, Block causes, Sinks, MCP profiles, skills, Framework adapters, Integration actions and triggers, Console screens). Each Feature is written `<kind>:<id>`, as ADR 0063's Journeys already write `row:CO-18`. Tests declare the Features whose outcome they assert, in each runner's own idiom; a check fails when a Feature has no test, and a Feature counts as tested only when every test that declares it passed on `main`'s latest Release suite run and none is quarantined. Code coverage and mutation testing are measured, never gated: their gaps are read in review and at each milestone gate.

> Amended by [ADR 0137](0137-the-console-leaves-both-products-and-the-engine-and-the-owners-monitoring-tool-is-designed-apart.md): no suite, test layout, Journey surface, security boundary, Performance budget, Feature kind (`screen:`) or actor exists for the Console.

The owner asked that "coverage means every feature is tested, not a percentage". Comparable projects prove it the same way, by walking a list ([findings](https://github.com/goodfetch/goodfetch/blob/research/journeys-traceability/rnd/research/2026-10-13-journeys-traceability.md), §3.2):
- **Kubernetes** compares the API operations its conformance run called, read from audit logs, with every GA endpoint of its OpenAPI spec; an endpoint with no test must be in `ineligible_endpoints.yaml` with a reason and a link. The measure is the set of untested endpoints, which must stay empty.
- **GitLab** makes every route, API endpoint, worker and RSpec example name a `feature_category` from a generated list, and a spec walks every route.
- **OpenFastTrace** fails its trace when a requirement lacks the coverage its type needs. **OpenTelemetry**'s compliance matrix, self-reported with no link to a test, is the case to avoid.
- **Patterns over-match.** web-platform-tests warns that a file pattern mapping tests to features silently captures unrelated new tests.
- **Runners carry IDs differently.** nextest has no tags, only names and paths; Vitest 4.1+ rejects undeclared tags by default; pytest rejects unknown markers only under `strict_markers`; Playwright's JUnit report drops tags.
- **On coverage and mutants:** Google's mutation testing runs only on changed code, during code review, with mutants filtered and capped so they stay actionable ([Petrović et al., IEEE TSE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.11378)). Google's testing blog does recommend per-commit coverage gates, while saying a high percentage "does not guarantee high quality" and that judgment over the uncovered lines matters more ([2020](https://testing.googleblog.com/2020/08/code-coverage-best-practices.html)); the owner's requirement rules the gate out and keeps the gaps.
- **Tools checked on 2026-10-13:** cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1 measures binaries spawned by any test through `show-env`; Vitest's `v8` provider measures Node and Chromium over CDP; cargo-mutants 27.1.0 has `--in-diff` and `--shard`; StrykerJS 10.0.0's Vitest runner still reports nearly every mutant as survived on Vitest 5 ([#6210](https://github.com/stryker-mutator/stryker-js/issues/6210) open, its three fix pull requests unmerged), while its `command` runner works with any test command at the cost of running every test for every mutant; mutmut 3.8.0 needs `fork`.

Decided in [Feature coverage and traceability](https://github.com/goodfetch/goodfetch/issues/279), with the grilling answered by the agent on the owner's delegation, on the facts of [Journey catalogs, test IDs and feature traceability](https://github.com/goodfetch/goodfetch/issues/269), [Rust test tooling in 2026](https://github.com/goodfetch/goodfetch/issues/263) ([findings](https://github.com/goodfetch/goodfetch/blob/research/rust-test-tooling/rnd/research/2026-10-13-rust-test-tooling.md)) and [Testing TypeScript and Python SDKs over a separate engine](https://github.com/goodfetch/goodfetch/issues/266) ([findings](https://github.com/goodfetch/goodfetch/blob/research/sdk-testing/rnd/research/2026-10-13-sdk-testing.md)). Suites are ADR 0061's, flaky tests and Live checks ADR 0064's, Journeys ADR 0063's. The rules every test follows are in `TESTING.md`.

## Decision

### What a Feature is

- **A Feature** is one behaviour Goodfetch promises, listed in the Feature inventory as `<kind>:<id>`. A Cargo feature is a different thing and keeps its full name.
- **Declared kinds**, written by people:

  | Kind | IDs | Source |
  |---|---|---|
  | `row:` | ADR 0037's matrix IDs (`row:RT-10`, `row:V3-05`, `row:durability-resume`), except `excluded` rows | the matrix file, read by `xtask codegen`; never copied |
  | `story:` | `story:<area>-<n>`, the spec's own story number (`story:2-56`) | `features/stories/<area number>.toml` |

- **Generated kinds**, read from the definition each contract already has:

  | Kind | One Feature per |
  |---|---|
  | `operation:` | Operation catalog operation |
  | `error:` | Error code |
  | `event:` | catalog event |
  | `setting:` | setting of the generated settings schema (ADR 0028) |
  | `command:` | CLI command path, from clap's `Command` |
  | `exit:` | exit code of `goodfetch-protocol`'s table (ADR 0069) |
  | `format:` | versioned format of the format registry (ADR 0066) |
  | `plugin-kind:` | Plugin kind (ADR 0033) |
  | `block-cause:` | Block cause |
  | `sink:` | built-in Sink |
  | `mcp-profile:` | MCP profile |
  | `skill:` | agent skill |
  | `adapter:` | Framework adapter |
  | `integration:` | Integration action or trigger (`integration:n8n/start-crawl`) |
  | `screen:` | Console route, read statically from the Console's route definitions in source |

  A new kind is added only by an ADR that amends this one. - **IDs.** Generated IDs are the contract's own name, so they change only when the contract does; a renamed contract is a change every declaring test must follow, which the check enforces. Story IDs are append-only, like Journey IDs (ADR 0063): a new story takes the next number of its spec, a removed one is `retired` with a `reason`, and a number is never reused.

### The inventory

- **One top-level `features/` folder**, beside `journeys/`:
  - `inventory.json`: every Feature with its kind, ID, area, milestone (declared kinds) and status, generated by `xtask codegen` and committed, so a pull request's diff shows each Feature it adds or removes (Kubernetes' golden list). `xtask codegen --check` fails on drift.
  - `stories/<area number>.toml`: each story's `id`, `title`, `milestone`, `journey` flag and `status`. The spec's issue keeps the full text; this copy is the one checks read, since they run under ADR 0043's deny.
  - `rows.toml`: each matrix row's milestone. The row list itself comes from the matrix.
  - `areas.toml`: the owning area of each generated Feature, by kind and ID prefix.
  - `exceptions.toml`: below.
- **The shapes are Rust types**, deserialized with `deny_unknown_fields`; `xtask codegen` emits their JSON Schemas beside them, as for the Journey type.
- **Area and milestone.** A generated Feature exists only once its code does, so it is due in the pull request that adds it. A declared Feature carries the milestone of the ticket that finishes it: it is *planned* before that milestone's gate and *due* from it.

### Declaring what a test proves

- **A test declares a Feature only when it asserts that Feature's outcome**, never one it merely passes through.
- **In each runner's idiom**, with no file patterns:
  - **Rust (nextest):** a doc line `/// Covers: operation:runs.start, error:run_not_found` on the test function, or `//! Covers: …` on a test module for every test in it. `xtask features` reads them with `syn` and maps them to nextest's test names, rstest cases included.
    > Agent decision, as built (#3149, 2026-11-21): a long `Covers:` declaration wraps onto the doc lines below it, each holding Feature IDs only; prose, a blank doc line or another attribute ends it. A test inside a macro the scan cannot read, such as `prop_state_machine!`, declares nothing yet (#3203).
  - **Vitest:** tags named by the Feature IDs, declared in the config from `inventory.json`, with `strictTags` on.
  - **pytest:** `@pytest.mark.covers("<feature id>")`, or `pytestmark` on a module, registered, under `strict_markers`; the test-support plugin lists them at collection.
  - **Playwright Test:** one annotation `{ type: "covers", description: "<feature id>" }` per Feature, read from `--list` with the JSON reporter.
  - **Journeys:** their `covers` list (ADR 0063), whose kinds are those above.
  - **Conformance suites and the Client conformance cases of `conformance/clients/` (ADR 0069):** a `covers` list on each case, beside its capability.
- **The exercise audit** checks the declarations a log can confirm, for tests that drive the protocol. For `operation:`, `error:` and `event:`, the records are those of `rpc`'s dispatch: each request's method and the Error code of its reply, and each event sent to a Client. Tests of the binary get them from the engine's JSON structured log (RT-17), which test support turns on into the test's Goodfetch home. In-process tests that send requests through the in-memory transport get them from the test `tracing` subscriber. For `command:` and `exit:`, test support's command helper records the command path and exit code. A protocol-driving test that declares one of these Features and never reached it fails the audit. No build of `goodfetch` gains a test switch (ADR 0059).
  > Agent decision, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-22 (#353): each test nextest runs under `just test pre-merge` or `release` leaves an exercise record in `target/test-records/`, one JSON-lines file whose first line names the test (`<binary id> <test name>`, from nextest's `NEXTEST_BINARY_ID` and `NEXTEST_TEST_NAME`) and whose other lines are `tracing`'s JSON lines: those `TestEnv` copies from the engine's log folder in its home when it drops, and those the test `tracing` subscriber writes under the dispatch target. A command record, which the CLI helper writes once it exists, is a line of target `goodfetch::test::command` with `command`, named as its `command:` Feature names it (`browsers.install`), and `exit_code`; an `exit:` Feature is reached when the code its entry has in the catalog's `exit_codes` table was seen. A declaring test with no record fails the audit as `record-missing`; the unit test of the next bullet is recognised as one at the `unit` level whose record holds no dispatch record. The audit reads only Rust tests' declarations until the TypeScript and Python packages write records (part 2 of the Test infrastructure spec). Corrected 2026-10-21: dropped the sentence saying the audit is not yet a suite step; it is, with the justfile's `exercise_audit := "gate"`.
  > Agent decision, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-21 (#365): the CLI helper writes each command line into the test's command record, `commands.jsonl` in its folder, which `TestEnv`'s teardown copies into the exercise record before the engine's logs. Its command is the longest run of the test's arguments whose names, joined by dots, are a `command:` Feature of the committed `features/inventory.json`, read when the command runs; arguments that hold none are recorded as `unmatched` (the arguments joined by spaces), and the audit fails each such line as `command-unmatched`, since no declaration can claim it. A test that starts the executable without the helper, as an Attached engine's tests do, records its command through `record_command`.
  > Agent decision, as built (#1779, 2026-10-30): a dispatch record can also come from the Client's side. The engine's log is lossy (ADR 0122), so an engine killed after an answer loses the dispatch records its writer's thread had not written yet, and the audit failed a test that had reached `run.export`. Flushing the log before each answer would slow every call, against ADR 0078. Instead, a test's Client of an engine that does not exit by itself, killed or left to teardown's kill, writes a dispatch record (method, and Error code when the call failed) for each call it read answered. It writes them into the test's answer record, `answers.jsonl` in its folder, which teardown copies after the command record. Test support's `AnsweredCalls` keeps these records, and Collie's and Foxhound's `Attached` helpers use it. An engine that exits by itself flushes its log at exit, so its own records stay the only ones.
  > Agent decision, as built (spec #325's review, M14, 2026-10-22): the exercise audit reads the declarations of Rust tests alone; a conformance case's or a Journey's `covers` list is not audited. Neither leaves an exercise record of its own: each conformance suite runs inside one nextest test, which declares the suite's Features on its own `Covers:` line and is audited against the suite's whole record, and each case's declaration counts as the outcome its kept `conformance` document gives the case; a Journey's declaration counts as its variants' result documents give them. A per-case record, which would let the audit judge each case's own `covers`, waits for the harness to write one.
- **A unit test that never reaches `rpc`** (a module's own error or event, asserted through its interface) may still declare the `error:` or `event:` Feature it asserts. The audit doesn't see it, so that test must assert the Error code or the event itself, as `TESTING.md` requires for every failure, and the fresh review checks that it does.
  > Amended by [ADR 0133](0133-agent-work-follows-the-matt-pocock-skills-as-written-and-the-fresh-review-is-retired.md): no fresh review exists; this check is a review standard the `code-review` skill applies, and the owner sees its result before merging.
  > Agent decision, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-21 (exercise audit wired into the Pre-merge suite, follow-up to #353; narrowed after spec #130's review): the rule holds for a test that never reaches `rpc`, as this bullet says, and for no other. The audit recognises one as a test whose record holds no dispatch record, or a unit test that left no record; a test above the unit level must still leave a record, so a missing one is `record-missing`, and a test whose record shows it dispatched is judged on every declaration, unit test or not. TESTING.md puts a module's test that binds a socket, such as the Browser cache's downloads against a loopback stand-in, in `tests/it`, though it never reaches `rpc` and asserts the module's own Error code and event as a unit test does, so it falls under the rule. An Error code a Run records and no reply carries, such as a work item's `handler_lost`, is reached rather than exempted: the engine writes an outcome record (target `goodfetch::run::outcome`, with the `error_code`) when its driver records one, the engine's JSON log and the test `tracing` subscriber carry it into the exercise record beside the dispatch records, and the audit reads it as the Error code reached. A declaration the audit finds unreached is fixed by reaching it, or by moving or removing it, never by widening this rule. Operations stay audited at every level. The suites' audit steps (#321) are the gate.

### What counts as tested

A Feature is **tested** when, on `main`'s latest Release suite run:
1. at least one test declares it;
2. every test that declares it ran and passed in every configuration it runs in, and none is on the quarantine list (ADR 0064);
3. every variant of a declaring Journey whose milestone has been reached is `proved` (ADR 0063); variants of later milestones don't count yet;
4. every declaring conformance case's capability is `proved` in its result document;
5. a story with `journey = true` also has a Journey that covers it.
   > Amended by [ADR 0075](0075-a-user-story-needs-a-journey-only-when-it-is-a-persons-goal-a-variant-can-reach.md): rule 5 is due at the later of the story's milestone and the earliest milestone of a covering variant, and every story also needs a declaring test above the unit level.

A Feature with an entry in `features/exceptions.toml` is **excepted**, by its evidence kind, unless it is also tested. Every other Feature is **untested**, with its cause: no test, failed, quarantined, or not run. Every test belongs to a suite (ADR 0061), so a declaring test the Release suite didn't run is a fault, not a skip. The gates fail only on untested Features: an excepted Feature passes them and is listed.
> Amended by [ADR 0074](0074-the-goodfetch-chromium-is-gated-where-it-is-built-against-a-control-build-of-the-same-revision.md): the Chromium build gate's tests are in no suite; they declare no Feature.

- **A unit test alone counts**, except for rule 5. `/to-spec` sets `journey = true` on stories whose actor is a person using Goodfetch (a user, an operator, an agent's user), and off on stories of contributors, maintainers and areas.
  > Amended by [ADR 0075](0075-a-user-story-needs-a-journey-only-when-it-is-a-persons-goal-a-variant-can-reach.md): `/to-spec` sets `journey = true` only on stories that pass its three tests (`actor`, `part`, `reach`), records the failed test as `not_journey` otherwise, and a story needs a test above the unit level.
- **A Feature is tested once, not once per surface.** Surfaces are generated from one catalog (ADR 0038), and the surface ADRs already require their own completeness: generated API completeness and every Client conformance case on every surface (ADR 0069), the MCP client matrix (ADR 0070), and a Journey on every surface it lists (ADR 0063).
  > Amended by [ADR 0094](0094-both-products-are-released-and-signed-together-and-each-test-runs-on-collie-unless-it-needs-foxhound.md): nor once per Product. The inventory records the Products that carry each Feature, and `xtask features report` gives each Product's view.
- **The check counts Features, not depth.** One test makes a Feature tested; depth comes from the stories, the review and the mutation signal.

### Exceptions

- **`features/exceptions.toml`** lists Features no pinned test in this repository can prove. Each entry has the Feature ID, an `evidence` kind, a `reason` and a `link`:
  - `manual`: needs a person; links the owner-test step or an ADR's manual test (the GUI MCP hosts of ADR 0070, LM Studio in ADR 0065);
  - `live`: its input can't be pinned; links the Live check or Evaluation that reaches it (ADRs 0064 and 0065);
  - `check`: met by repository configuration and checked by a named CI job, not by a product test (an area 1 story such as `cargo-hack` checking every feature combination); links the job;
  - `none`: no test in this repository reaches it, such as an Error code only Goodfetch Cloud returns; links where it is tested.
- **An exception is never counted as tested:** its Feature is excepted, a status of its own, and the report shows each evidence kind apart. It is never allowed for a Feature a pinned test can reach; the fresh review checks the reason.
  > Amended by [ADR 0133](0133-agent-work-follows-the-matt-pocock-skills-as-written-and-the-fresh-review-is-retired.md): no fresh review exists; this check is a review standard the `code-review` skill applies, and the owner sees its result before merging.
- **No pending list.** ADR 0064's quarantine already covers a test that exists but can't be trusted yet.

### The checks

| Check | Where | Fails when |
|---|---|---|
| Feature check (static) | Quick suite | the inventory is stale; a declaration names an unknown or retired Feature; a generated Feature has no declaring test and no exception; a non-excluded matrix row has no milestone; a generated Feature maps to no area or to two; an exception lacks a field, names an unknown Feature, or names a Feature a test also declares |
| Exercise audit | Pre-merge suite (tests that ran), Release suite (all tests) | a declaring test never reached its `operation:`, `error:`, `event:`, `command:` or `exit:` Feature |
| Milestone gate | the owner test of ADR 0058 | any generated Feature, or any declared Feature due at the milestone, is untested (neither tested nor excepted) on `main`'s latest Release run |
| Release gate | `xtask release` | any Feature present in the release is untested (neither tested nor excepted) |

> Agent decision, as built (#338): until `features/rows.toml` gives the matrix rows their milestones, the Feature check does not fail on a row without one, and the inventory lists such a row with no milestone. No ticket has set the rows' milestones yet, so the rule would fail every pull request; it is switched on in the change that fills `rows.toml`.

> Agent decision, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-21 (#351): the Vitest tags, Playwright annotations and pytest markers come from the runners' listings, which start processes, and a Quick-suite check starts none (ADR 0061). The Feature check therefore reads them in the Pre-merge suite (`just features-tests`, after `just journeys-tests`, on the same listings), where every rule above applies. In the Quick suite it reads the Rust `Covers:` lines and the Journeys' and conformance cases' `covers` lists, applies every rule but one, and only notes a generated Feature none of them declares, since a runner's test may declare it.

> Verified on 2026-10-19 (#351): Vitest 5.0.5 accepts `:`, `.`, `/`, `-` and `_` in tag names, in the configuration, on a test and in `--tags-filter`, so Feature IDs are its tags as written and no mapping exists.

> Agent decision, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-21 (#321): the Pre-merge and Release suites run the exercise audit with the verdict the justfile's `exercise_audit` names. It is `report` until the declarations #353's first run found unreached are fixed (#321's report lists them): the audit then lists its findings and fails nothing, so it does not yet fail "all green". Setting it to `gate` makes it the check of the table above. Set to `gate` once the follow-up to #353 brought the findings of a whole-workspace Pre-merge run to none (agent decision, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-21).

> Agent decision, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-21 (spec #130's review): "all tests" in the Release suite is each cell's own nextest run, which runs every test but the quarantined ones (ADR 0064) and those the cell cannot run. Each cell's audit therefore reads the tests that run's JUnit file shows ran, as the Pre-merge suite's does, so a quarantined declaring test, which leaves no record, never fails a cell, as ADR 0064 says a quarantine never fails a run. The audit reads nextest's JUnit file where nextest writes it, `target/nextest/ci/junit.xml` under the workspace (never under `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`), and fails when tests left records but no JUnit file names them, so it never passes without reading. `just features-audit all`, every declaring test whether it ran or not, stays for a local look.

> Agent decision, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-21 (#321): the milestone gate's state is the Feature report's `gate` (whether it is ready, and the untested Features' IDs) and its last line; it is ready only when the store holds a Release run of `main`. The daily test-health job writes it to its job summary.

- **Before the merge queue exists**, the Release suite runs on manual dispatch (ADR 0061), and the two gates read the latest such run on `main`.
  > Amended by [ADR 0108](0108-while-the-repository-is-private-the-release-suite-runs-its-macos-cells-on-the-owners-machine-and-its-hosted-cells-under-a-ceiling.md): while the repository is private, "the latest such run" is `main`'s latest commit whose cells have all run, across its dispatches; a commit some of whose cells have not run yet is not read.
- **The release pull request lists every exception**, with its evidence kind.

### Code coverage: measured, never gated

- **A coverage job in no suite**, on Linux x64, weekly while ADR 0032's nightly tier is off and nightly once it is on. While the repository is private, it has a 60-minute timeout, and its minutes count toward ADR 0064's ceiling of 1,000 included minutes a month under a lower threshold of their own: the coverage job and the in-diff mutation job run only while the month's count is below 550 minutes, which leaves ADR 0064's expected 450 minutes to its own runs.
  - Rust: cargo-llvm-cov over nextest, plus every SDK, Journey and Console run against the instrumented binary through `show-env`;
    > Amended by [ADR 0137](0137-the-console-leaves-both-products-and-the-engine-and-the-owners-monitoring-tool-is-designed-apart.md): no Product carries a Console, so what this says of the Console ends; the rest stands.
  - TypeScript: Vitest's `v8` provider, on Node and in Browser Mode;
  - Python: coverage.py with branch measurement, under pytest.
- **No threshold**: no `--fail-under-*`, no percentage in any gate, badge or pull request, and no coverage service.
- **It is read for gaps.** The report lists the functions no test executes, per crate and package, beside the feature report. A gap that hides a behaviour with no Feature becomes a story, a Feature or a test. Each milestone's gate issue links the latest report.
- **Verdicts never come from an instrumented build.** Its results are stored under their own configuration and never decide a Feature's status.
- **`just coverage`** runs it locally over what changed.
  > Agent decision, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-21 (#321): the coverage job is `.github/workflows/coverage.yml`, on Saturdays and by hand. Its tests' JUnit files carry the runtime `instrumented`, so the results store keeps them as a configuration of their own and the flaky-test scan never compares them with an uninstrumented run; its step is not a test step. cargo-llvm-cov builds into a target folder of its own, and test support passes `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE` to every executable a test starts.
  > Agent decision of 2026-11-02 (#1879, as built), under ADR 0140's `coverage.project` ratchet: a `compare` job after the coverage job, holding the issue token and running none of the product, compares the project's line coverage with the Quality register's row within 0.5 % of the row's figure, and keeps one `needs-triage` issue when it falls. It fails no check and no merge, so "no percentage in any gate" stands.

### Mutation testing: read in review, never scored

- **Rust, every pull request that changes Rust code:** cargo-mutants `--in-diff` with nextest on Linux x64, sharded to fit ADR 0061's 15-minute job budget, in a job outside the suites that never fails on a surviving mutant. It is not part of "all green", the one required check (ADR 0061), so a slow shard never delays the merge signal. Its report is attached to the run. While the repository is private, it runs at most four shards of 15 minutes per pull-request run, and it stops at the same 550-minute threshold as the coverage job; a pull request whose job was skipped says so in its Verification section.
  > Amended by [ADR 0135](0135-while-the-repository-is-private-the-owners-machine-runs-the-pull-request-tier-in-a-throwaway-linux-vm-and-private-fuzzing-nightly.md): while the repository is private, it runs on the owner's machine with the pull-request tier, using no included minutes, without the four-shard cap or the 550-minute threshold.
  > Amended by [ADR 0133](0133-agent-work-follows-the-matt-pocock-skills-as-written-and-the-fresh-review-is-retired.md): the section is the `pr` skill's Evidence section.
- **The pull request's Verification section lists each mutant that survives in its changed code**, with the test that now kills it or the reason it stays: an equivalent mutant, or one caught only by a doctest, by a Journey in another runner, or by another OS's test (cargo-mutants doesn't read `cfg(target_os)`). The fresh review checks the list.
  > Amended by [ADR 0133](0133-agent-work-follows-the-matt-pocock-skills-as-written-and-the-fresh-review-is-retired.md): the section is the `pr` skill's Evidence section, and checking each reason is a review standard the `code-review` skill applies.
- **Full runs, weekly once the nightly tier is on:** cargo-mutants sharded over the workspace; StrykerJS on the TypeScript SDK's hand-written runtime and the Console's logic; mutmut on the Python SDK's hand-written runtime, on Linux. Stryker uses its `command` runner until a release fixes #6210, then its Vitest runner, and the TypeScript packages then gain the same in-diff pull-request job as Rust.
  > Agent decision, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-21 (#321): the in-diff job's shard count comes from the `affected` job, one shard per 4 mutants `cargo mutants --list` gives for the change (`ci/mutants.sh`), to be retuned from the recorded durations. Mutants are tested in the job's own checkout (`--in-place`), with nextest skipping what `just test` skips; the test tool manifest's executables are built before the first mutant, so a mutant reaches one only when its package's test build rebuilds it, and one only an SDK or Journey test would kill may survive there. The full runs are not built while the nightly tier is off.
  > Amended by [ADR 0137](0137-the-console-leaves-both-products-and-the-engine-and-the-owners-monitoring-tool-is-designed-apart.md): no Product carries a Console, so what this says of the Console ends; the rest stands.
  > Agent decision, as built (#3097): StrykerJS 10.1.0 fixed #6210, so the full run uses StrykerJS's Vitest runner from its first configuration, `sdks/typescript/stryker.config.mjs`, and never the `command` runner. Its Vitest configuration leaves out one Client conformance case, `nothing-at-import-or-connect`, which StrykerJS's instrumentation fails by design (it reads a variable and adds a global at import); `just test` keeps running it. mutmut's configuration is each Python SDK package's `[tool.mutmut]`. `just mutants-sdks` runs both, and neither mutates a `generated/` folder (ADR 0099). The TypeScript in-diff job is #3192. Neither run yet mutates what a test's child process imports or skips the quarantined tests (#3199), so a mutant reached only through a child program reads as untested.

  > Agent decision, as built (#3199): both runs now reach the programs a test starts. StrykerJS mutates the sources in place and mutmut's copy is first on the child's `PYTHONPATH`, so a child imports the mutated code; what it lacks is the run's state, which test support hands it. A Node program started through the process record gets the active mutant in `__STRYKER_ACTIVE_MUTANT__`, or, while StrykerJS learns coverage, preloads a module that writes each mutant it covers to a file, counted for the test that started it (`mutation-children.ts`); the config turns Vitest's `related` off, since a test that reaches `collie/src/bin.ts` only through the program it starts imports nothing mutated. Under `--mutation-children`, a Python program started with the runner's environment or `test_env`'s map imports a `sitecustomize` that writes each function it reaches to a file, which the plugin gives the test before mutmut's own teardown hook, and makes `warnings.warn` not count mutmut's trampoline frames, so a warning still names its caller's line. A program started any other way is not reached. The quarantine skip comes from `xtask quarantine exclude`: pytest's `--deselect`s, named from each package's `mutants/` copy, through `PYTEST_ADDOPTS`, and Vitest's pattern through a setup file, since StrykerJS sets Vitest's own name pattern.

  > Agent decision, as built (#3192): the TypeScript in-diff job is `just mutants-typescript [base]`, which runs by hand, as the Rust one does while its pull-request workflow is off. `ci/mutants-typescript.sh` turns each hunk of the committed runtime changes since the base into a StrykerJS mutation range (`<file>:<first>-<last>`, HEAD's lines) and passes them as `--mutate` through the full run's config, so it mutates only those lines, never a test or a `generated/` file, and refuses uncommitted runtime changes, which would move the lines. StrykerJS tests a mutant only when it lies wholly within one range, so a mutant spanning unchanged lines, such as the body around a changed line, is left out. Its in-place backups go to `.stryker-tmp/` beside the sources, since StrykerJS restores them by renaming, which fails across volumes. Both runs list their survivors, and the mutants no test reaches, in their report folder's `summary.md`; neither fails on one. It runs every mutant at once, unsharded: the TypeScript runtime's changes stay small.
- **No mutation score is published or gated.** A full run's survivors are a list, read at each milestone gate.

### Reports

- **`xtask features report`** joins the inventory, the declarations and ADR 0064's results store. For each area and each milestone it gives the Features tested, untested (by cause), excepted (by evidence kind) and planned, and for each untested Feature its declaring tests with their last outcomes.
- **The daily test-health job (ADR 0064) builds it** as JSON for agents and an HTML page beside the Allure report, and writes each run's report into the `test-results` repository, so coverage has a history.

  > Agent decision, as built (spec #325's review, H4, 2026-10-22): while ADR 0135 keeps the test-health workflow off, `just reports <store>` builds the daily Feature report, and the Journey report with the next owner test's "Journeys to try", run daily by the server's cron on `main`'s head. It commits each day's reports into the `test-results` checkout under `reports/<date>/` and pushes them, after the secret scan.
- **Each milestone's owner test** lists its `manual` exceptions as manual steps, and links the feature, coverage and mutation reports.
- **`just features`** runs the static Feature check locally and prints what the changed packages declare and miss.

### Ownership

- **Generated Features need no one to list them:** they appear with their code, and the Quick check fails until a test declares them.
- **Each area's `/to-spec`** writes its `features/stories/<area number>.toml` in its `/to-tickets` pull request or the first ticket's, with each story's `journey` flag. **`/to-tickets`** sets each story's and each row's milestone, and names in each ticket the Features it makes tested.
  > Amended by [ADR 0133](0133-agent-work-follows-the-matt-pocock-skills-as-written-and-the-fresh-review-is-retired.md): no skill writes repository files or ticket fields. The stories file (each story's flags and milestone) and the Journeys of flagged stories must exist before a test declares them; tickets add them like any other work.

## Considered Options

- **ADR 0037's rows alone as the inventory:** rejected. 171 rows hide most settings, Error codes and events; a row passes on one test while they stay untested.
- **User stories alone:** rejected. They are hand-kept, and an Error code added by a ticket appears in none.
- **A percentage of code covered, or a mutation score:** rejected by the owner's requirement. Both stay as measurements.
- **Counting only what the audit observes, with no declaration** (Kubernetes' endpoint audit alone): rejected. Every test that passes through an operation would cover it, the over-capture web-platform-tests warns of.
- **A mapping file per package by test-name pattern** (web-platform-tests' `WEB_FEATURES.yml`): rejected. The link sits away from the test, and patterns capture unrelated new tests.
- **A `#[covers]` attribute macro in Rust:** rejected. It needs a proc-macro crate for a line a scanner reads as well; unknown IDs fail the Quick check either way.
- **Runtime annotations written into JUnit:** rejected. nextest can't write them, and Playwright's JUnit report drops tags.
- **Reading the spec issues' stories from GitHub in a job:** rejected. It is one more exception to ADR 0043's deny, and the check would depend on state outside the commit.
- **Every Feature tested on every surface:** rejected. The surfaces are generated from one catalog; the per-surface completeness, Client conformance and Journey variants already prove each surface.
- **A test at every level for every Feature:** rejected. It duplicates what the pyramid avoids (ADR 0063).
- **A test-management service's traceability matrix** (Qase): rejected for ADR 0063's reasons: outside review, outside ADR 0043's deny, invisible to people who rerun the Proving ground.
- **Codecov or another coverage service:** rejected. A vendor outside the deny for a number nothing gates on.
- **Mutation testing only in scheduled full runs:** rejected as the only form. Google's evidence is that mutants are actionable on changed code during review; whole-tree lists go unread.
- **Waiting for Stryker #6210 before any TypeScript mutation run:** rejected. The `command` runner measures now, only slower.

## Consequences

- **Adds to ADR 0038**, so ADR 0037's amendment rule carries it to every area's spec: each area's `/to-spec` writes its stories into `features/stories/`, with their `journey` flags; `/to-tickets` sets each story's and row's milestone and names in each ticket the Features it makes tested; story numbers are append-only.
  > Amended by [ADR 0133](0133-agent-work-follows-the-matt-pocock-skills-as-written-and-the-fresh-review-is-retired.md): no skill writes repository files or ticket fields. The stories file (each story's flags and milestone) and the Journeys of flagged stories must exist before a test declares them; tickets add them like any other work.
- **Adds to ADR 0032:** the `features/` folder at the root of the repository; the coverage job and the mutation jobs.
- **Amends ADR 0032** (a note there records it): while the repository is private, the weekly coverage job and the pull-request in-diff mutation job run too, within ADR 0064's ceiling of included minutes.
- **Amends ADR 0064's ceiling** (a note there records it): it also counts the coverage job and the in-diff mutation job, which stop once the month's count reaches 550 minutes, so they never take the minutes of ADR 0064's own runs.
- **Adds to ADR 0030's release gates:** `xtask release` refuses while a Feature present in the release is untested, and the release pull request lists every exception.
- **Amends ADR 0058's readiness rule a second time** (a note there records it): an owner test is also ready only when every generated Feature, and every declared Feature due at its milestone, is tested or excepted on `main`'s latest Release run. Its "Journeys to try" gain the milestone's `manual` exceptions.
- **Adds to ADR 0063:** the Feature kinds `covers` may name are this ADR's; the catalog check's "whether `covers` names existing features" is the Feature check. Its deferrals to [Feature coverage and traceability](https://github.com/goodfetch/goodfetch/issues/279) (the Feature kinds, whether `covers` names existing features, the inventory and the "every feature is tested" check) are decided since in this ADR.
- **Adds to ADR 0069:** each Client conformance case has a `covers` list. Its "Mutation testing: not decided" is decided since in this ADR.
- **Adds to ADR 0070:** its Integration actions and triggers and its Framework adapters are the `integration:` and `adapter:` kinds (assumed there).
- **Adds to ADR 0061:** the Feature check in the Quick suite; the exercise audit in the Pre-merge and Release suites. The coverage and mutation jobs are in no suite, and the Rust in-diff mutation job is outside "all green"; its shards keep to the Pre-merge per-job budget of 15 minutes.
- **Changes the specs of areas 1 to 3** through the delta pass: each gains its `features/stories/<area number>.toml` from its user stories; area 1 builds the checks and jobs; area 2's conformance suites and Client conformance cases carry `covers`; area 3's structured log records each RPC request's method and Error code and each event's type as fields. ADR 0037's area table lists this ADR in the rows of areas 1 and 2.
- **The glossary** gains *Feature* and *Feature inventory*.
- **The "Test infrastructure" spec builds:** the inventory types and their schemas, `xtask features` (scanner, check, exercise audit, report), the generators of each kind (the static read of the Console's routes included), the Vitest tag configuration (mapping IDs one to one if Vitest's tag names refuse `:` or `.`, which is unverified), the pytest and Playwright listings, the command helper's record, the coverage job, the mutation jobs, and the report page. It watches StrykerJS #6210.
  > Amended by [ADR 0137](0137-the-console-leaves-both-products-and-the-engine-and-the-owners-monitoring-tool-is-designed-apart.md): no Product carries a Console, so what this says of the Console ends; the rest stands.

> Corrected on 2026-10-19 in [#370](https://github.com/goodfetch/goodfetch/issues/370): the coverage and in-diff mutation jobs start only while the month's count is below 550 minutes, so a run that starts just below can pass 550 by up to its timeout; they leave ADR 0064's expected 450 minutes to its own runs, rather than never taking them.
